# Provenance and Limits Stated Inline

The boundary of a claim is written **next to the claim**, not in a footnote or an appendix. Confirmed
in 13 of 15 repositories and unusually strong in five. This is the habit that makes the source set
trustworthy despite [[documentation-drift]] elsewhere.

## Evidence

> "No deploy command has been run against a live account from this environment — you run them
> yourself with your own accounts."
> — browser_game_stickfps/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, 2026-07-25

> "// For this dataset: if any bridge exists, κ'(G) = 1; otherwise treat as 2 (a conservative
> placeholder — a full Stoer-Wagner cut is out of scope)."
> — Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/lab5_GraphTheory/SentinelNet/sn-algo.js, 2026-06-09

## The forms it takes

**A negative result advertised in the headline.** `Optimization Methods` puts its blind GA *losing*
to a greedy heuristic in the README's own comparison table, under the heading "Two modifications
(**one negative, kept honest**)". See [[blind-baseline-comparison]].

**A typed provenance field.** `Farley` carries `CarSpec.source = "built-in" | "fueleconomy.gov" |
"estimate"`, `VisionResult.method = "cloud" | "on-device"`, and merges its event calendar by
precedence `live > listing > typical`. Provenance is a value in the type system, not a comment.

**Naming the variant not used.** `Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence` implements the
simple-moving-average RSI and names Wilder's exponential smoothing as the variant it did *not* use —
see [[relative-strength-index]].

**Scoping what the work is not.** `Research Methodologies` states its benchmark table is "not
experiments run for this coursework"; `Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories` has a dedicated "A
note on scope"; `privacy-policy` says "not legal advice"; `Physics` marks its Node tools "not shipped
to the browser".

**Self-reported doc bugs.** `Optimization Methods/final_project/docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md` flags that
`HOW_TO_RUN.md` "names two scripts that don't exist" — recording the defect rather than fixing it.

**Retroactive labelling.** `browser_game_stickfps/PROGRESS.md` marks one round entry "logged
retroactively during the round-9 documentation pass — reconstructed from the shipped code", and
separates harness quirks from product bugs by name.

**Reproducibility stated as a limit.** `Optimization Methods` reports that fresh OpenStreetMap
downloads no longer reproduce the paper's distances because "OSM has drifted" — a negative
reproducibility result kept in the audit rather than quietly dropped.

## The counter-current

The habit is strongest **deep** in a repo and weakest at the top. `Farley`'s `lib/*.ts` headers state
scope and fallback behaviour meticulously while its public README claims a test suite that does not
exist. `labour-fraud-analysis` has the most developed threat model in the set *and* a README claim
("test-verified in CI") that overstates what CI enforces, since the leak scan skips on a clean
runner. Depth correlates with honesty; the guided tour in
[[readme-as-guided-tour]] is where accuracy is thinnest.
